A01.name: urban street

timeline.text: Target: the car initially approaching from the bottom of the opening frame in the inner incoming lane, facing upward; follow this same car as it turns toward the left side of the image. Event: its first left turn through the intersection. Onset: its body heading first changes from its initial straight-ahead orientation. Offset: its heading finishes changing and settles along the outgoing road toward image-left. Forward travel with unchanged heading before or after the turn is outside this interval; do not time another car or the moment it crosses a road marking.

events.action: Track the cars approaching in the straight-through lanes of the four road arms, separately from the cars in the inner left-turn lanes. Their crossing begins as they enter the junction and continues straight across it with body heading aligned to the incoming road.
events.outcome: The same straight-through cars reach the opposite road arms with no left-turn heading change; progress of a turning car does not satisfy this event.

events.action: Track the cars initially approaching in the inner lanes from the bottom, right, top and left of the intersection. Each left turn begins when that car starts changing heading, follows a curved path across the junction, and ends when its heading settles along its perpendicular outgoing road. The bottom-entry car turns toward image-left.
events.outcome: The turning cars complete their heading changes and advance along their respective outgoing road arms; straight approach or crossing a stop line alone is not a completed turn.

end_state: Cars have progressed away from their opening positions along their assigned roads.
The road layout remains fixed while the cars move.
A01.target_context: Track the cars approaching in the straight-through lanes of the four road arms, separately from the cars in the inner left-turn lanes. Their crossing begins as they enter the junction and continues straight across it with body heading aligned to the incoming road. Track the cars initially approaching in the inner lanes from the bottom, right, top and left of the intersection. Each left turn begins when that car starts changing heading, follows a curved path across the junction, and ends when its heading settles along its perpendicular outgoing road. The bottom-entry car turns toward image-left.

A02.name: billiards table

timeline.text: Target: object ball 1 in the initially compact group of billiard balls, near the lower/front edge of that group in the opening view, identified by its numbered patch when visible; not the incoming cue ball. Event: this same ball is displaced by the break. Time: the first crossing of 0.03 scene units of distance from its own opening position, not the cue-ball launch, another ball moving, or completion of rack dispersal. This is a single displacement-threshold crossing, with no separate end boundary.

events.action: Track the incoming cue ball and the initially compact group of numbered object balls. The break begins with the cue ball reaching the group and transferring motion through ball contacts; follow the object balls as the group opens.
events.outcome: Several object balls separate from their opening neighbors and move away from the compact group; cue-ball travel without disruption of the group is insufficient.

events.action: Track the numbered object balls originally in the compact group, not just the cue ball. After the break, they roll away on distinct paths and may contact one another or the cushions.
events.outcome: The original group has become a spatially dispersed arrangement on the table; camera motion or a single ball moving while the group stays compact does not count.

end_state: The original compact rack has dispersed.
The visible balls remain on the table surface.
A02.target_context: Track the incoming cue ball and the initially compact group of numbered object balls. The break begins with the cue ball reaching the group and transferring motion through ball contacts; follow the object balls as the group opens. Track the numbered object balls originally in the compact group, not just the cue ball. After the break, they roll away on distinct paths and may contact one another or the cushions.

A03.name: jar-packaging equipment

timeline.text: Target: the narrow retractable metering stop across the bottle conveyor at the downstream end of the held bottle queue, not a bottle or the fixed machine frame. Event: the stop retracts downward to let bottles advance. Onset: the stop itself first moves downward relative to the conveyor. Offset: that downward stroke ends at its lowered position. Bottle motion before or after this stroke is not a boundary of the stop motion.

events.action: Track the upright bottles queued on the moving belt through the fixed packaging frame. Follow their advance as the retractable stop lowers and releases the queue, then as bottles pass the machine section.
events.outcome: The same bottles have advanced along the belt relative to the fixed guides and machine, with subsequent bottles occupying earlier positions; frame motion or stop motion alone is not bottle transport.

end_state: A line of upright bottles remains on the conveyor.
Different bottles occupy the visible section compared with the opening.
A03.target_context: Track the upright bottles queued on the moving belt through the fixed packaging frame. Follow their advance as the retractable stop lowers and releases the queue, then as bottles pass the machine section.

A04.name: sailboats

timeline.text: The sailboats move laterally across the lake on distinct courses. Track each sailboat by its hull and mast from its opening location on the lake. During the observed sailing interval, hulls advance on distinct courses relative to the water and shore; the interval is continuous rather than a single launch or docking action. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

The boats continue sailing past one another with their hulls and masts remaining upright. Track each sailboat by its hull and mast from its opening location on the lake. During the observed sailing interval, hulls advance on distinct courses relative to the water and shore; the interval is continuous rather than a single launch or docking action. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

events.action: Track each sailboat by its hull and mast from its opening location on the lake. During the observed sailing interval, hulls advance on distinct courses relative to the water and shore; the interval is continuous rather than a single launch or docking action.
events.outcome: Individual boats occupy changed locations while retaining distinct hulls and upright masts; apparent displacement caused only by camera motion does not establish sailing.

end_state: Several boats remain upright on the water.
Their arrangement has changed from the opening fleet arrangement.
A04.target_context: Track each sailboat by its hull and mast from its opening location on the lake. During the observed sailing interval, hulls advance on distinct courses relative to the water and shore; the interval is continuous rather than a single launch or docking action.

A05.name: carousel

timeline.text: The carousel carries the horses around the central axis. Track the horses attached to the carousel poles around the fixed central axis. Observe their changing angular positions as the platform carries them around; motion is already ongoing and no unique startup or stop is required. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

The horses rise and fall along their vertical poles while being carried around the carousel. Track individual carousel horses relative to their own vertical poles while the platform rotates. A bobbing cycle rises from a local low height, reverses at a high height and descends again; judge height along the pole rather than image position. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

events.action: Track the horses attached to the carousel poles around the fixed central axis. Observe their changing angular positions as the platform carries them around; motion is already ongoing and no unique startup or stop is required.
events.outcome: The horses advance around the axis while remaining on their own poles; vertical bobbing without angular travel does not satisfy rotation.

events.action: Track individual carousel horses relative to their own vertical poles while the platform rotates. A bobbing cycle rises from a local low height, reverses at a high height and descends again; judge height along the pole rather than image position.
events.outcome: Horse heights change along their poles and different horses can occupy different heights while staying attached; rotation alone does not establish bobbing.

end_state: The horses remain attached to their poles and arranged in rings.
The carousel structure remains assembled.
A05.target_context: Track the horses attached to the carousel poles around the fixed central axis. Observe their changing angular positions as the platform carries them around; motion is already ongoing and no unique startup or stop is required. Track individual carousel horses relative to their own vertical poles while the platform rotates. A bobbing cycle rises from a local low height, reverses at a high height and descends again; judge height along the pole rather than image position.

A06.name: pendulum apparatus

timeline.text: The suspended balls swing back and forth about their fixed upper attachment points. Track the suspended pendulum balls beneath the fixed support rail, each associated with its own suspension point. Follow successive swings through the center and reversals at the sides rather than treating the whole array as a rigid object. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

The pendulums continue swinging with changing relative phases rather than moving as one rigid group. Track the suspended pendulum balls beneath the fixed support rail, each associated with its own suspension point. Follow successive swings through the center and reversals at the sides rather than treating the whole array as a rigid object. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

events.action: Track the suspended pendulum balls beneath the fixed support rail, each associated with its own suspension point. Follow successive swings through the center and reversals at the sides rather than treating the whole array as a rigid object.
events.outcome: The balls change their relative arrangement through back-and-forth motion while the upper suspension points stay fixed; a camera sweep is not an oscillation.

end_state: The balls remain suspended from the support rail.
The support frame stays stationary while the balls move.
A06.target_context: Track the suspended pendulum balls beneath the fixed support rail, each associated with its own suspension point. Follow successive swings through the center and reversals at the sides rather than treating the whole array as a rigid object.

A07.name: balloon-themed Ferris wheel

timeline.text: The wheel rotates, carrying gondolas along its circular rim. Track the passenger gondolas attached around the Ferris-wheel rim, relative to the fixed hub and support legs. The rotating wheel carries them along circular paths while each basket retains an upright passenger orientation; no unique start or stop is expected. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

The gondolas continue around the wheel while their passenger baskets remain upright. Track the passenger gondolas attached around the Ferris-wheel rim, relative to the fixed hub and support legs. The rotating wheel carries them along circular paths while each basket retains an upright passenger orientation; no unique start or stop is expected. This phase is an observation window, not a claim of a unique physical startup or stop; assess the described motion relative to its support throughout the shown frames.

events.action: Track the passenger gondolas attached around the Ferris-wheel rim, relative to the fixed hub and support legs. The rotating wheel carries them along circular paths while each basket retains an upright passenger orientation; no unique start or stop is expected.
events.outcome: The same gondolas reach changed angular locations around the hub and remain attached with baskets upright; camera motion alone is insufficient.

end_state: The gondolas remain attached around the wheel rim.
The passenger baskets remain upright.
A07.target_context: Track the passenger gondolas attached around the Ferris-wheel rim, relative to the fixed hub and support legs. The rotating wheel carries them along circular paths while each basket retains an upright passenger orientation; no unique start or stop is expected.

A08.name: marble-run apparatus

timeline.text: Track the marbles initially distributed among the stacked funnels. Follow each marble as it rolls around a funnel and progresses through its outlet into a lower part of the apparatus. Marbles reach funnel levels below their own opening levels. Finishing in a collection tray is not required because the evaluated reference clip does not show tray contact.

events.action: Track the marbles initially distributed among the stacked funnels. Follow each marble as it rolls around a funnel and progresses through its outlet into a lower part of the apparatus.
events.outcome: Marbles reach funnel levels below their own opening levels. Finishing in a collection tray is not required because the evaluated reference clip does not show tray contact.

end_state: The marbles are at lower levels of the apparatus than at the beginning.
A08.target_context: Track the marbles initially distributed among the stacked funnels. Follow each marble as it rolls around a funnel and progresses through its outlet into a lower part of the apparatus.

B01.name: tabletop dominoes

timeline.text: Target: the first upright domino at the starting end of the curved single row, initially at the upper-left end in the opening view; track this block rather than its neighbor. Event: the initiating block tips and transmits the fall into the row. Time: the first instant its tilt exceeds five degrees from its opening upright orientation. Do not use contact with the next block or the time it lies flat; this event has one threshold-crossing boundary.

Target: the last domino at the opposite end of the curved single row, initially at the right-hand end in the opening view. Event: the propagating cascade reaches this terminal block and it starts tipping. Time: this block first exceeds five degrees of tilt from its opening upright orientation. Earlier blocks falling or this block finally lying flat do not define the time; there is one crossing boundary.

events.action: Track the first domino at the starting end of the curved single row, initially at image upper-left, and its immediate neighbor. The event starts when the first block tips, then contacts the next block and initiates adjacent toppling.
events.outcome: The next blocks begin falling in order while blocks farther down the row are still upright; merely moving the whole row or tipping an unrelated terminal block is insufficient.

events.action: Follow the chain of adjacent dominoes from the already triggered starting end along the curve to the terminal block at image-right. Each falling block transfers the fall to its next neighbor.
events.outcome: Toppling reaches the terminal end while earlier blocks remain down; simultaneous unrelated collapse without propagation along the row does not establish the described cascade.

end_state: The whole domino row is toppled.
The fallen dominoes remain down.
B01.target_context: Track the first domino at the starting end of the curved single row, initially at image upper-left, and its immediate neighbor. The event starts when the first block tips, then contacts the next block and initiates adjacent toppling. Follow the chain of adjacent dominoes from the already triggered starting end along the curve to the terminal block at image-right. Each falling block transfers the fall to its next neighbor.

B02.name: Newton's cradle

timeline.text: Target: the hand initially holding the raised rightmost ball of the five-ball Newton cradle. Event: the hand withdraws outward from that ball to release it. Onset: the hand begins its first outward withdrawal from the held position. Offset: this outward withdrawal stops. Track hand translation, not the ball reaching the central row, the leftmost ball swinging, or the later return of the hand to catch the rightmost ball.

events.action: Track the initially hand-held raised rightmost ball and the opposite leftmost ball of the five-ball cradle. After the hand withdraws, the rightmost ball swings inward and strikes the central row.
events.outcome: The leftmost ball swings outward after the incoming strike while the middle balls remain approximately centered; the release alone is not the completed exchange.

events.action: Track the leftmost ball that swung outward after the first strike, and follow it back toward the central row. The return exchange begins with its inward swing and collision with the row.
events.outcome: The rightmost ball swings outward again after the return strike; do not substitute its initial held pose or first release.

events.action: Track the hand and the same rightmost cradle ball that was initially held. After the free swings, the hand returns to intercept that ball near its raised position.
events.outcome: The hand holds the raised ball and its free swinging stops; a brief natural turning point without being held is not a catch.

end_state: The hand holds the rightmost ball raised.
The other balls hang approximately at the central resting position.
B02.target_context: Track the initially hand-held raised rightmost ball and the opposite leftmost ball of the five-ball cradle. After the hand withdraws, the rightmost ball swings inward and strikes the central row. Track the leftmost ball that swung outward after the first strike, and follow it back toward the central row. The return exchange begins with its inward swing and collision with the row. Track the hand and the same rightmost cradle ball that was initially held. After the free swings, the hand returns to intercept that ball near its raised position.

B03.name: bowling equipment

timeline.text: Target: the single front/head pin at the apex of the bowling-pin formation facing the approaching ball, centered ahead of the other pins. Event: this pin tips after the ball arrives. Time: its first tilt exceeding five degrees from its opening upright orientation. Do not substitute first ball-pin contact, sliding without tilt, another pin falling, or the head pin reaching the floor. Only this crossing is timed.

events.action: Track the bowling ball approaching along the lane and the single front/head pin at the apex facing it. The impact begins when the ball reaches the front of the pin formation and makes contact.
events.outcome: The front pins start tilting or translating from their initial positions after the contact; a ball passing nearby without disturbing them is insufficient.

events.action: Track the pins initially arranged behind the head pin. After the initial ball impact, contacts propagate through this group and individual pins topple or slide apart.
events.outcome: Most pins end down and at least one remains upright, matching the reference outcome; ball travel alone or only the head pin moving does not satisfy this event.

end_state: Most pins are lying down at the end of the lane.
At least one pin is still standing.
B03.target_context: Track the bowling ball approaching along the lane and the single front/head pin at the apex facing it. The impact begins when the ball reaches the front of the pin formation and makes contact. Track the pins initially arranged behind the head pin. After the initial ball impact, contacts propagate through this group and individual pins topple or slide apart.

B04.name: marble-loop apparatus

timeline.text: Target: the marble initially at the lower inlet beside the vertical elevator on the right of the apparatus (Marble_01); follow this same marble as the lift raises it to the top. Event: it transfers from the lift onto the descending return track. Onset: its world height first starts decreasing after the upward ride. Horizontal motion or the elevator mechanism rotating is not this boundary; only the start of descent is scored.

events.action: Track a marble carried by the vertical elevator on the right of the loop apparatus. Follow it upward to the top exit and across the connection onto the upper descending track.
events.outcome: That same marble leaves the lift and continues along the upper return track; an empty lift moving or a different marble already on the track is insufficient.

events.action: Track a marble on the lower return track as it approaches the bottom inlet of the right-hand elevator. The receiving interval begins at its approach to the inlet and ends as the lift accepts it.
events.outcome: The marble enters the elevator receiving position rather than rolling off the end of the track; upper-track transfer is a different event.

end_state: Marbles are still moving on the apparatus near the end.
The lift continues carrying marbles upward.
B04.target_context: Track a marble carried by the vertical elevator on the right of the loop apparatus. Follow it upward to the top exit and across the connection onto the upper descending track. Track a marble on the lower return track as it approaches the bottom inlet of the right-hand elevator. The receiving interval begins at its approach to the inlet and ends as the lift accepts it.

B05.name: excavator and dump truck

groups.bed: Bed floor|Dump bed side(?:\.\d+)?|Bed end gate(?:\.\d+)?

timeline.text: Target: the excavator upper carriage carrying its cab, boom and bucket, rotating on the stationary lower chassis beside the dump truck. Event: its first swivel toward the truck after loading the bucket. Onset: the upper carriage first changes yaw toward the truck. Offset: this yaw rotation stops at its truck-facing orientation. Boom raising, bucket curling and soil falling are separate motions and must not set these yaw boundaries.

events.action: Track the excavator bucket at the end of the boom and the soil beneath it, distinct from the nearby dump truck. The bucket enters or curls through the soil and is then raised from the ground.
events.outcome: Soil is visibly carried inside the raised bucket; an empty bucket lifting is not the completed scoop-and-lift event.

events.action: Track the same loaded excavator bucket as the upper carriage swivels from the digging area toward the nearby truck bed. Above the bed, the bucket tips outward to discharge its contents.
events.outcome: Soil leaves the bucket and falls into the truck bed; carriage rotation without dumping or soil falling beside the truck does not establish loading.

end_state: The bucket has left its tipped unloading pose.
The excavator has begun turning back toward the digging side.
B05.target_context: Track the excavator bucket at the end of the boom and the soil beneath it, distinct from the nearby dump truck. The bucket enters or curls through the soil and is then raised from the ground. Track the same loaded excavator bucket as the upper carriage swivels from the digging area toward the nearby truck bed. Above the bed, the bucket tips outward to discharge its contents.

B06.name: canal drawbridge

groups.leaves: Left lifting bridge leaf|Right lifting bridge leaf
groups.cars: First crossing car|Final eastbound car|Final westbound car

timeline.text: Target: the movable bridge leaf on the left half of the canal crossing in the opening view, attached to its bank hinge; not a car or the boat. Event: its first opening stroke from the horizontal road position. Onset: the leaf first rotates upward about its hinge. Offset: that upward rotation ends at its raised position. A car leaving the bridge or the boat entering the gap is not the leaf boundary.

Target: the same bank-hinged left bridge leaf used for bridge opening. Event: its first downward closing stroke from the raised position toward the road. Onset: the leaf starts rotating downward. Offset: its downward rotation ends at the closed road position. Do not use the boat passing or cars restarting as the boundary; observe the leaf angle itself.

events.action: Track the first road car approaching the drawbridge while the hinged leaves are still horizontal and connected. Follow that car onto and across the bridge deck.
events.outcome: The same car reaches the opposite bank before the opening stroke; the later post-closing traffic is a separate event.

events.action: Track both hinged bridge leaves and the boat approaching through the canal. The sequence starts with the leaves rotating up to open the water passage, then the boat travels through the gap.
events.outcome: The boat clears the space under the bridge while the leaves are still raised, before they begin lowering; opening alone is insufficient.

events.action: Track the raised drawbridge leaves and the road cars waiting at the banks. The leaves rotate down until their road surfaces reconnect, after which cars advance onto the deck.
events.outcome: Road cars cross on the reconnected closed deck; cars moving before the bridge closes do not establish successful restoration.

end_state: Both bridge leaves are closed and form a continuous road.
Cars are crossing the restored roadway.
B06.target_context: Track the first road car approaching the drawbridge while the hinged leaves are still horizontal and connected. Follow that car onto and across the bridge deck. Track both hinged bridge leaves and the boat approaching through the canal. The sequence starts with the leaves rotating up to open the water passage, then the boat travels through the gap. Track the raised drawbridge leaves and the road cars waiting at the banks. The leaves rotate down until their road surfaces reconnect, after which cars advance onto the deck.

B07.name: cargo-loading equipment

groups.cargo: Pallet and cargo — same continuous load

timeline.text: Target: the forklift front moving carriage and its pair of L-shaped forks beneath the loaded pallet, not the vehicle chassis or truck. Event: the first upward fork stroke carrying the pallet. Onset: the fork carriage starts rising relative to the mast. Offset: that upward stroke stops at the raised level. Driving the forklift forward, moving the camera, or later withdrawing the forks does not extend this vertical-motion interval.

events.action: Track the forklift moving fork carriage and the loaded pallet above its forks, relative to the mast and the nearby truck bed. The event starts with the forks rising and ends at the raised loading height before forward insertion.
events.outcome: The pallet is supported by the forks at a height that clears the truck bed; forklift translation without vertical lifting is insufficient.

events.action: Track the same pallet as the forklift carries it into the truck, lowers it onto the bed, and reverses with its forks withdrawing from beneath it.
events.outcome: The pallet and cartons stay supported on the truck bed while the forklift backs away; carrying the pallet back out is not successful unloading.

end_state: The pallet of cartons remains inside the truck.
The forklift is separated from the deposited load as it reverses away.
B07.target_context: Track the forklift moving fork carriage and the loaded pallet above its forks, relative to the mast and the nearby truck bed. The event starts with the forks rising and ends at the raised loading height before forward insertion. Track the same pallet as the forklift carries it into the truck, lowers it onto the bed, and reverses with its forks withdrawing from beneath it.

B08.name: packaging conveyor

timeline.text: Target: the leading carton nearest the downstream end of the output rollers (Carton 1), followed continuously from its opening position as other cartons queue behind it. Event: its final forward movement during accumulation. Offset: its last forward translation ends and it remains at that position for the rest of the clip. An earlier temporary pause is not the final stop, and movement of an arriving carton is not movement of this target. Only the final offset is scored.

events.action: Track the leading carton initially nearest the downstream output side of the packaging machine. It advances out onto the roller section and decelerates relative to the fixed roller frame.
events.outcome: Its forward translation noticeably slows; movement of the belt, camera or a following carton is not evidence that this leading carton slowed.

events.action: Track the leading carton and the following cartons emerging from the machine. Each arriving carton catches up to the one ahead and the resulting contacts advance the queue before it settles.
events.outcome: The cartons form a closely packed queue that is approximately stationary near the end; separated moving cartons or a single temporary pause do not establish the accumulated queue.

end_state: The cartons form a closely packed queue on the output rollers.
The queue is approximately stationary.
B08.target_context: Track the leading carton initially nearest the downstream output side of the packaging machine. It advances out onto the roller section and decelerates relative to the fixed roller frame. Track the leading carton and the following cartons emerging from the machine. Each arriving carton catches up to the one ahead and the resulting contacts advance the queue before it settles.

C01.name: model railway

timeline.text: Target: the leading coach of the connected train, the first coach to enter the tunnel; keep this coach identity through disappearance and reappearance. Event: its first almost-complete tunnel occlusion. Onset: the visible fraction of this coach drops to at most 10 percent. Offset: its visible fraction first rises above 10 percent as it emerges. Initial partial covering and the last trailing coach entering or exiting do not define these boundaries.

events.action: Track the connected train from its leading coach as it approaches the entrance tunnel portal. The leader passes inside, then successive coaches follow into the same opening and become blocked by the tunnel.
events.outcome: The train becomes hidden by the tunnel structure in coach order; passing in front of the tunnel facade is insufficient.

events.action: Track the same train through the tunnel interval and identify its leading coach reappearing at the other portal. Subsequent coaches follow it onto the outgoing track.
events.outcome: Connected coaches are visible on the right-hand outgoing track; a different train or visibility at the entrance portal is not the specified exit.

end_state: The train is visible outside the right tunnel portal.
Its coaches remain connected in sequence.
C01.target_context: Track the connected train from its leading coach as it approaches the entrance tunnel portal. The leader passes inside, then successive coaches follow into the same opening and become blocked by the tunnel. Track the same train through the tunnel interval and identify its leading coach reappearing at the other portal. Subsequent coaches follow it onto the outgoing track.

C02.name: bridge and boats

timeline.text: Target: Ferry 1, the boat initially nearest the left end of the bridge on the lower/near side of its deck in the opening view, heading toward the passage beneath the bridge. Track this same boat, not one on the opposite side or farther right. Event: its first almost-complete bridge occlusion. Onset: at most 10 percent of the target remains visible behind the bridge. Offset: more than 10 percent becomes visible again beyond the obstruction. Passing a bridge edge with most of the boat still visible is not the onset.

events.action: Track the passenger boats approaching the bridge on the water, preserving each boat identity through the deck occlusion. Each underpass begins with approach beneath the deck, continues through hiding, and ends with emergence on the other side.
events.outcome: The same boats reappear beyond the bridge and continue on the water; passing alongside the bridge without going beneath it does not count.

end_state: Boats remain upright on the water on both sides of the bridge.
The bridge remains fixed while the boats change position.
C02.target_context: Track the passenger boats approaching the bridge on the water, preserving each boat identity through the deck occlusion. Each underpass begins with approach beneath the deck, continues through hiding, and ends with emergence on the other side.

C03.name: revolving-door entrance

timeline.text: Target: the torso of the single walking person approaching the revolving-door enclosure from image-left; track the torso, not the head, legs or a door panel. Event: the torso becomes almost fully blocked by the rotating door structure and then reappears. Onset: at most 10 percent of the torso is visible. Offset: the visible torso fraction first exceeds 10 percent again. The person starting to walk, entering the doorway, or finally leaving the entire enclosure are different boundaries.

events.action: Track the single walking person approaching the revolving-door enclosure from image-left, distinct from its rotating panels. The person moves into a door compartment while the panels rotate around the central axis.
events.outcome: The door structure blocks the person from view during passage; rotation of an empty door or a person staying outside is insufficient.

events.action: Track the same person through the revolving-door enclosure after entry. Follow the person as the rotating compartment carries the passage toward the far opening.
events.outcome: The person emerges outside on the right and moves away from the door; a brief glimpse through a panel gap while still inside is not completed exit.

end_state: The person is visible outside to the right of the door.
The revolving-door structure remains in place.
C03.target_context: Track the single walking person approaching the revolving-door enclosure from image-left, distinct from its rotating panels. The person moves into a door compartment while the panels rotate around the central axis. Track the same person through the revolving-door enclosure after entry. Follow the person as the rotating compartment carries the passage toward the far opening.

C04.name: cable cars

timeline.text: Target: the cable-car cabin initially at the left of the opening view (Cable car 1), followed along its route; do not switch to the cabin initially on the right. Event: this cabin first becomes almost completely occluded along the route, then reappears. Onset: at most 10 percent of its target cabin geometry remains visible behind scene obstructions. Offset: the visible fraction first exceeds 10 percent again. Partial overlap with foliage or supports alone is insufficient.

events.action: Track each cable-car cabin along its fixed cable route, preserving its identity as foliage or other scene structures cover it. Follow the interval from approach to the obstruction through hiding to reappearance.
events.outcome: The same cabins become visible farther along the cable while staying attached to the route; another cabin entering view does not establish reappearance of the hidden one.

end_state: The two cabins remain on the elevated cable route.
Their positions along the route have changed.
C04.target_context: Track each cable-car cabin along its fixed cable route, preserving its identity as foliage or other scene structures cover it. Follow the interval from approach to the obstruction through hiding to reappearance.

C05.name: warehouse equipment

timeline.text: Target: the forklift initially at image-left of the warehouse, tracked as one vehicle behind the racks; do not follow the shelving or a carton on it. Event: its first almost-complete occlusion by the shelving and stored goods. Onset: at most 10 percent of the forklift target remains visible. Offset: its visible fraction first exceeds 10 percent again. Do not wait for the whole vehicle to clear the rack or time the beginning of driving.

events.action: Track the single forklift initially at image-left in the warehouse aisle. It drives behind the shelving and stored goods, becomes occluded, and continues toward the right-hand opening.
events.outcome: The same forklift emerges on the right beyond the racks; a carton moving or a view through a rack gap without passage does not establish aisle traversal.

end_state: The forklift is visible on the right side of the shelving.
The shelving and stored cartons remain stationary.
C05.target_context: Track the single forklift initially at image-left in the warehouse aisle. It drives behind the shelving and stored goods, becomes occluded, and continues toward the right-hand opening.

C06.name: elevated roadway

timeline.text: Target: the rigid upper load platform supported by the scissor arms above the fixed base, not an individual arm or hose. Event: the platform completes its first upward stroke. Target: the same rigid upper scissor-lift platform above the fixed base. Event: its second upward stroke, after the first rise and intervening lowering. Onset: its height starts increasing from the intervening low turning point. Offset: that second increase ends at the next local maximum. Count upward strokes of this platform; do not substitute its first rise or a later cycle.

events.action: Track the rigid load platform above the scissor linkage and fixed base. The first cycle raises the platform as the links open, reaches a high turning point, then lowers as the links fold.
events.outcome: The platform changes height upward and downward while remaining level and connected to the base; translation of the whole lift is insufficient.

events.action: Track the same platform after its first up-and-down cycle. It begins a second upward stroke from the intervening low point, reaches another high point, and lowers again.
events.outcome: The platform returns toward a low height with the scissor links still connected; replaying only the first rise or judging another moving part does not establish repetition.

end_state: The platform is near a low position above the base.
The crossed arms remain connected at their pivots.

E06.name: sponge

groups.sponge_and_basin: (?:Wet sponge • reduced compressible continuum|Hollow receiving basin)

timeline.text: Target: the sponge block above the receiving basin, judged by its top-to-bottom height, not a water droplet or basin edge. Event: the first sustained decrease in sponge height. Onset: that first downward compression starts. Offset: height reaches its first local minimum before recovery. Sideways bulging or droplets appearing does not define the boundary; track thickness rather than whole-object translation.

Target: the same sponge block above the basin. Event: the upward height segment after the first compression, which is the second increasing-height segment overall because a small initial expansion precedes the compression. Onset: height starts increasing from the first compressed minimum. Offset: this recovery ends at the next local maximum height. Do not count the opening expansion as this recovery or use droplets as a boundary.

events.action: Track the sponge block above the basin by its top-to-bottom height. During the first compression its height decreases to a local minimum, then increases during recovery; sideways bulging can accompany compression.
events.outcome: The sponge recovers height after the squeeze instead of merely translating as a rigid block; the receiving basin and droplets are not the deforming target.

events.action: Track the same sponge and the space between it and the basin during the subsequent squeeze. Compression deforms the sponge and visible droplets separate from it and travel downward.
events.outcome: Droplets fall below the sponge toward the basin receiving area; sponge deformation without released droplets does not establish this water-release outcome.

end_state: The sponge has expanded toward its wider shape.
The basin remains beneath the sponge.
